video-all-about-lights-0g1tqknlc2i-youtu.title: Hardwired LED Ceiling Light: Wiring a New Fixture with a Wall Switch
video-all-about-lights-0g1tqknlc2i-youtu.summary: This Old House's Ask This Old House episode demonstrates upgrading a ceiling lighting situation by replacing a cord-hung fixture with a hardwired LED fixture controlled from a wall switch. The crew identifies hazards of the old setup, plans a new ceiling box and a switch location, routes power from a convenient junction box to the wall switch, and then from the switch to the ceiling fixture. They pull wires with fish tape, splice neutrals, connect hot to the switch, and bond the ground, using Madison bars to secure boxes. The LED fixture is described as having a driver that converts house power to low voltage, producing bright light at a low 18-watt consumption, and weighs about two pounds. The result is a flush-mounted, switch-controlled ceiling light that eliminates the prior hanging hazard and makes the room feel larger.

video-all-about-lights-1scxy6oeu2u-youtu.title: All About Pendant Lights: Installing and Centering a 3-Pendant Kitchen Light (This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-1scxy6oeu2u-youtu.summary: This Old House's pendant-light installation guide walks through planning and executing a three-pendant setup above a kitchen peninsula. The segment covers determining structure and ceiling-box placement, upgrading a two-gang box to a three-gang with a dimmer, pulling and routing new wiring from the attic via a switch leg, labeling conductors, and wiring the three pendants with pigtails. It also shows centering the pendants using countertop measurements and a plumb-bob, drilling pilot holes, securing pancake boxes, sealing the top plate per code, and finally mounting the canopies. The video emphasizes practical wiring tasks (hot/neutral/ground identification, Romex handling, wire nuts) and retrofit mounting considerations for multiple fixtures on a single circuit.

video-all-about-lights-2ecfluuvqwk-youtu.title: Ultra-Thin LED Exterior Recessed Lighting Installation (Ask This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-2ecfluuvqwk-youtu.summary: The video demonstrates replacing an older, bulky recessed exterior light with a new ultra-thin LED recessed fixture. It explains the benefits of low-voltage operation (24V) derived from a 120V supply, and shows practical installation steps under a soffit, including mounting with clips and accommodating the soffit’s thickness. A key instructional focus is routing wiring to satisfy box capacity limits when adding multiple fixtures, followed by finishing with a digital astronomical wall switch to automate exterior lighting and a power-on reveal that highlights improved door illumination.

video-all-about-lights-37pzurgtmj8-youtu.title: All About Lights: Recessed Light Installation (This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-37pzurgtmj8-youtu.summary: This Old House demonstrates a practical attic-to-ceiling recessed lighting install. The episode covers selecting a lighting location away from obstructions, drilling clean access holes, running Romex 14-2 between fixtures, and mounting remodel housings with plaster-clips. It contrasts quick push-in wire connections with traditional twisting and wire nuts, shows grounding and neutrals being tied in a junction box, and ends with a test of the new recessed lights. The workflow emphasizes dust control, cable length planning, and safe termination of an unused conductor from the switch loop.

video-all-about-lights-4talvrw2n-u-youtu.title: Replacing a Post Light: Aluminum Post, LED Diode Fixture, and Time-Clock Control
video-all-about-lights-4talvrw2n-u-youtu.summary: This Old House documents a front-yard lighting upgrade focused on replacing a failing exterior post light. After identifying a faulty wall switch and a deteriorating lamppost, the project replaces the post with a 7-foot aluminum model, installs a new LED diode fixture (no replaceable bulb) with a diffuser, and routes wiring through the post using dry-mix concrete for a quick-set footing. The update includes upgrading the electrical box to a weatherproof unit, pulling new wiring to a weatherproof outdoor switch, and installing an astronomical time clock to automate dusk-to-dawn lighting. To finish, the installer replaces a matching wall sconce to harmonize with the new post light. The video emphasizes durability, weatherproofing, and a cohesive exterior lighting design that complements the house and railing.

video-all-about-lights-7-yi5jebntc-youtu.title: Handmade Chandelier Assembly: Hook Forging, Arm Forming, Soldering, and Antique Brass Finish
video-all-about-lights-7-yi5jebntc-youtu.summary: This Old House follows a homeowner through a shop that handcrafts chandeliers and other fixtures. The episode centers on a custom eight-arm dining-room chandelier, detailing sequence—from initial design notes and parts overview to the actual fabrication steps (hook forging, arm forming, and soldering bobeche), through a multi-step finish (cleaning, acid etch, color application) and final electrical wiring. The piece is described as handmade-to-order with a living antique-brass finish, and the team notes a roughly three-week turnaround. The segment emphasizes craftsmanship, consistency across arms, and the integration of the fixture with home hardware and patina over time.

video-all-about-lights-9e1vmyj6ibs-youtu.title: Channel Letters with Jimmy DiResta: Template, Edge Wrapping, and LED Sign Assembly
video-all-about-lights-9e1vmyj6ibs-youtu.summary: Jimmy DiResta demonstrates a hands-on build of a backlit channel-letter sign. The project starts from a laser-cut logo template, then glue-tits are attached to plywood and cut into letters with a bandsaw (or a jig saw as an alternative). A circle-template guides even LED light distribution across all letters, followed by edge-wrapping each letter with aluminum flashing, and assembling the pieces with hot glue, nails, and spacers to hide wiring. The interior faces are primed, painted (on both sides), and the LED strips are installed from the back, sealed with silicone for durability, before a final power-test reveal. The video emphasizes practical, accessible techniques for custom channel-letter signage using common shop tools and inexpensive materials.

After the changes, a test shows all lights come on together, the basement appears brighter, and a claim is made about reduced electricity usage and heat with the LED upgrade.

The host walks through planning, power routing with a floating feed, cutting track to length, pre-assembling connectors, mounting with toggle bolts in a non-structural ceiling, wiring the track, installing individual fixture heads, and finally adding a pendant with an LED bulb and dimmer, highlighting LED efficiency advantages.

video-all-about-lights-chhegbf0baw-youtu.title: Wireless wall-switch retrofit using an in-fixture wireless receiver (Ask This Old House)

The approach avoids routing new conductors by using a wireless transmitter/receiver pair to operate the light, and it highlights common site constraints when routing wiring (attic access, wall notching, structure).

An outdoor LED lighting example emphasizes high light output with low power consumption. Throughout, the emphasis is on energy efficiency, controllability, and real-world applicability of LEDs in diverse settings.

video-all-about-lights-e4qtyatcmr0-youtu.title: Add Task Lighting to a Kitchen: Recessed Downlights and Under-/Over-Cabinet Fluorescents
video-all-about-lights-e4qtyatcmr0-youtu.summary: This Old House guides a kitchen-lighting upgrade in a small, low-light kitchen by replacing two ceiling fluorescents with recessed downlights and by adding task lighting from under and over the upper cabinets. The crew navigates a ceiling obstruction (a bar for a former junction box) and a sprinkler-pipe drop, uses a template to size openings, and hides cords by trimming the cabinet face with an oscillating saw. The result is improved lighting on the workspace and a more ambient glow on the ceiling, demonstrated toward the end as the cabinet lights are tested along with the recessed cans.

video-all-about-lights-gqszuiasyxc-youtu.title: Layering Light in the Kitchen: Planning, Layering, and Bulb Choices
video-all-about-lights-gqszuiasyxc-youtu.summary: This video demonstrates a practical approach to kitchen lighting through a three-layer strategy: general lighting to illuminate main paths, task lighting for prep areas, and accent lighting for style. It guides viewers to begin with a lighting plan or layout, then add recessed or surface-mounted general lighting, followed by under-cabinet task lighting, and finally decorative accent lighting such as pendant fixtures. The discussion covers coordinating fixture styles with cabinetry and plumbing, selecting bulb color temperatures (soft white for warmth, daylight for color accuracy), and the importance of consulting a licensed electrician for wiring. Overall, the guide emphasizes planning first, layering light, and choosing bulbs and fixtures that suit the kitchen’s design and function.

video-all-about-lights-gtczsbxpide-youtu.title: Recessed Lighting for a Slanted Ceiling: Layout, Wiring, and Aiming
video-all-about-lights-gtczsbxpide-youtu.summary: This Old House demonstrates a recessed lighting install for a room with a slanted ceiling, emphasizing layout accuracy, safe access, and directional control. The crew uses a laser aligned to the front edge of installed cabinets and chalk lines on an unpainted ceiling to maintain a straight, continuous line for the light run. Hole locations are identified by piercing plaster with a screwdriver and marking a 3-1/4 inch target while ensuring at least four inches of clearance before cutting with a hole saw. Wiring is run as a continuous loop and connected with push-in connectors (no wire nuts), with black-to-black and white-to-white terminations. A gimbal eyeball fixture is installed to allow tilt and wash, secured with mounting clips, and oriented for adjustable coverage. The session ends with planning for additional lights in the kitchen to achieve full lighting coverage.

video-all-about-lights-hqt08no9ksy-youtu.title: Hybrid Smart Lighting: Back-Plate Switch + Wireless Remote
video-all-about-lights-hqt08no9ksy-youtu.summary: The video explains three main pathways for smart lighting: upgrading an existing wall switch to a smart switch, using smart bulbs, or employing a hybrid approach that combines a back-plate module with a wireless remote. It covers what each option offers—local control (on/off), dimming, and app or voice assistant integration—and the tradeoffs, including the electrical work required for switches and the constant power needs of smart bulbs. The hybrid solution keeps the wall switch always on while adding a wireless remote for local control and dimming, with the caveat that power continues to flow to the light socket even when the light is off. Practical guidance is provided on when to choose a given approach, considering reliability, safety, and convenience.

video-all-about-lights-hxhcovjct1e-youtu.title: Copper French Quarter Gas Lantern Installation in St. Louis (This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-hxhcovjct1e-youtu.summary: This This Old House episode documents the exterior installation of a copper, New Orleans–inspired (French Quarter) gas lantern on a building in St. Louis. The team describes the lantern’s design cues (copper construction, fleur‑de‑lis motifs), plans routing a gas line from an interior source to the exterior, and coordinates with a licensed gas fitter and the local gas utility. The project proceeds with panel access to conceal the line, masonry drilling to pass the line, and running a 1/4‑inch copper tube down the wall to the basement before mounting the lantern on a gooseneck bracket, purging the line, and lighting a decorative pilot flame. The video emphasizes safety, planning, and the aesthetic integration of a classic lantern in a Midwestern urban setting, with a nighttime payoff anticipated.

The segment emphasizes energy efficiency (LEDs consuming about half a watt per bulb, totaling less than a single 60-watt equivalent) and concludes with a test lighting up the deck. The lesson balances practical wiring techniques with safety considerations and a visually appealing outcome suitable for outdoor entertaining.

Safety features highlighted include a cable locked twice on the roller and a key-controlled, slow operation. The sequence covers attic access to the box, converting the box area to mount the lift, and testing the system by raising the fixture to demonstrate illumination and maintenance adjustments.

The plan centers on hidden LED tape running along the beams to create a bright, indirect glow, while pendant lighting and careful mounting strategies are evaluated to avoid visual clutter and respect the historic structure.

video-all-about-lights-knzyinxdsva-youtu.title: Installing Concealed Lighting
video-all-about-lights-knzyinxdsva-youtu.summary: This video shows a kitchen lighting upgrade that emphasizes concealed, ceiling-preserving solutions alongside decorative pendant lighting. To illuminate the island, three pendant fixtures are mounted using a sturdy local box as the anchor, mindful of the island’s geometry and canopy projection to keep the fixture centers aligned. To light the adjacent living area without recessed ceiling lighting, the crew adds LED tape along the tops of the beams to create uplighting and ambient illumination. The LED tape is installed inside an aluminum channel in a routed groove, with five-foot segments joined end-to-end, wired to terminal blocks, and covered with a diffuser to soften the light. The team tests brightness, verifies even coverage across the island and surrounding space, and discusses remaining accent lighting to complete the look.

video-all-about-lights-kxc5itnfwn4-youtu.title: How to Install a Motion-Activated Security Light
video-all-about-lights-kxc5itnfwn4-youtu.summary: This Old House illustrates a DIY exterior lighting upgrade by installing a motion-activated security light. video-all-about-lights-kzcf4nasyew-youtu.title: Choosing Recessed Light Bulbs: Incandescent, Halogen, CFL, and LED
video-all-about-lights-kzcf4nasyew-youtu.summary: This video from This Old House compares common recessed-light bulb options, explaining what each bulb type is, how it’s installed in recessed fixtures, and practical considerations such as heat, ballast technology, upfront cost, lifespan, and long‑term energy savings. It covers incandescent, halogen (MR16), compact fluorescent (CFL) with a four-pin plug-in, and LED recessed lights. The hosts note that electronic ballasts reduce CFL flicker and buzz, describe LED as a circuit-board light source, and contrast initial price against longevity and electricity use, highlighting LED’s substantial efficiency advantage despite higher upfront cost.

video-all-about-lights-llczyxsklyw-youtu.title: Orange U-Shaped LED Light and Edge-Cutting Light: A Quick Demo Pack from Ask This Old House

video-all-about-lights-lozervu7yku-youtu.title: Diagnosis and Repair of a Miswired Three-Way Switch (This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-lozervu7yku-youtu.summary: The video demonstrates a common three-way switch setup where two switches control a single light. The presenter distinguishes single-pole switches from three-way switches, defines the common (black) terminal and the two traveler (brass) terminals, and uses a cutaway to illustrate how a single-pole switch normally completes a circuit. The core of the lesson focuses on diagnosing a miswiring in the dining-room circuit where the common and traveler wires were swapped, likely due to an improper homeowner replacement. After tracing conductors (black and red) from two cables in the box, the speaker shows that the red traveler was tied to the common screw and the black common wire was tied to a brass traveler screw. The fix involves swapping these two wires and ensuring proper screw wrap direction. After restoring power, both switches correctly operate the light, confirming the repair.

video-all-about-lights-p0ta45tefqe-youtu.title: Diagnosing and wiring a three-way light switch (Ask This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-p0ta45tefqe-youtu.summary: In this episode, This Old House guides a homeowner through diagnosing a miswired three-way switch arrangement that controls a chandelier from two locations. The hosts explain the difference between single-pole and three-way switches, describe the role of traveler wires and the common, and demonstrate a practical workflow: turn off power, remove the switches, identify traveler vs. common conductors, use a continuity tester to locate the travelers, wire the two travelers to the traveler terminals and the common to the common terminal, reconnect the ground, restore power, and test from both switch locations. The lesson emphasizes wiring theory applied to a real-world scenario, safety steps, and the value of diagrams to understand a three-way circuit while avoiding common miswiring mistakes.

video-all-about-lights-rngcwfg7ohm-youtu.title: How to Convert a Recessed Light to a Pendant
video-all-about-lights-rngcwfg7ohm-youtu.summary: This Old House demonstrates converting a recessed can light into a pendant using a dedicated conversion kit. The host explains why a direct swap is impractical due to the existing ceiling box and structure, then walks through assembling and mounting a socket adapter, hollow support rod, and mounting plate attached to the can. The kit uses decorative medallions to cover the large recessed opening and blends with the ceiling. The wiring is connected from the socket to the pendant (hot/black, neutral/white, ground/green), the traditional fixture bar is removed, and the pendant is assembled and tested with an LED bulb to ensure an aesthetically pleasing, energy-efficient result. Safety steps include shutting off power at the breaker and carefully tucking wires inside the canopy before finishing.

video-all-about-lights-tbrfygrzceg-youtu.title: Installing an Antique Gas-Light Fixture: Wiring, Box Mount, and LED Retrofit
video-all-about-lights-tbrfygrzceg-youtu.summary: This Old House demonstrates installing an antique Victorian gas-light fixture converted to electric, focusing on safe wiring and ceiling-mount considerations in a setting with exposed components and limited attic access. The hosts identify hazards in the existing setup (three-conductor BX cable, no dedicated ground, exposed splices) and outline a plan to mount a metal junction box using a mounting bar, re-route wiring through a new ceiling opening, and splice the fixture to the circuit. The process includes removing an obstructing gas pipe, using anti-short bushings and grounding clamps, and completing the installation with an antique-style push-button switch that incorporates a dimmer and LED bulbs designed to mimic an original glow. The overall emphasis is on safely integrating old and new elements while preserving the fixture’s historic appearance.

video-all-about-lights-tj8scph2ou8-youtu.title: Cable Lighting Installation: Low-Voltage Ceiling Rails (Ask This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-tj8scph2ou8-youtu.summary: This This Old House segment demonstrates upgrading a long, narrow room from dated track lighting to a low-voltage cable lighting system. The presenter explains using a ceiling-mounted transformer to deliver 12-volt power across two ceiling cables, supported by standoffs, with a 35-watt halogen fixture that can be positioned along the run. The installation workflow shown includes mounting the transformer, extending wiring, measuring and mounting standoffs with toggle bolts into plaster, threading the cable through end eyelets, and testing the system. The result is bright, perimeter lighting with a rainbow-like fixture appearance that enhances room brightness and perceived size.

video-all-about-lights-ubtfpmdkqus-youtu.title: Surface-Mounted LED Downlights Retrofit with Wireless Dimming
video-all-about-lights-ubtfpmdkqus-youtu.summary: The video documents upgrading four bright dome ceiling lights in a living room by introducing a surface-mounted LED fixture that mimics recessed lighting without drywall demolition. The host contrasts four common recessed lighting paths—new construction housings, old-work housings with drywall clips, and a four-inch recessed box—and demonstrates a surface-mount option that preserves ceiling integrity while providing even light distribution. After installation, the plan shifts to dimming control across a two-location, three-way setup: replacing one switch with an electronic dimmer and adding a battery-powered wireless dimmer remote at the opposite location to enable dimming and on/off control from either side, with a bypass of the existing switch wiring to enable seamless operation.

video-all-about-lights-umdhjbfe1ju-youtu.title: Understanding the Lighting Facts Label: Lumens, Wattage, Kelvin, and Integrated LEDs
video-all-about-lights-umdhjbfe1ju-youtu.summary: This short educational segment explains how to read the Lighting Facts label on modern light bulbs. It emphasizes lumens as the brightness metric, clarifies that wattage represents power consumption rather than brightness, and provides practical comparisons (e.g., 800 lumens roughly equals a 60-watt incandescent). It then introduces color temperature in the Kelvin scale, noting that lower numbers feel warmer while higher numbers feel cooler, with 2700–3000 K suggested for a traditional look. The video concludes by noting the rise of integrated LED fixtures, which carry the same label and can last 20 years or longer, underscoring the value of reading and understanding the label when shopping for lighting.

video-all-about-lights-uw-wpyas4ps-youtu.title: Shopping for Lighting: Dining Room Pendants and Island Fixtures with This Old House
video-all-about-lights-uw-wpyas4ps-youtu.summary: In this This Old House segment, homeowners Derek and Robin consult a lighting designer, Kimberly, while shopping in a showroom to outfit a full-house renovation. The video follows their process of establishing a focal point in the dining room, evaluating fixture styles from contemporary to traditional, and exploring pendant configurations, glass finishes, and canopy options. Key moments include sizing guidance tied to the dining table length, sampling of glass finishes (smoke, clear, frosted, rose gold), and planning three pendants over the kitchen island to coordinate with cabinetry. The segment emphasizes the value of seeing fixtures in person in a showroom, leveraging professional advice, and converging on a cohesive lighting plan that ties dining room and island lighting together.

video-all-about-lights-zbebljyoflc-youtu.title: Installing an Overhead Light with a Wall Switch in a Master Bedroom (Ask This Old House)
video-all-about-lights-zbebljyoflc-youtu.summary: This Old House demonstrates a complete overhead-light installation in a master bedroom, including center-layout planning to maximize usable space, locating and wiring a switch leg from an existing circuit, cutting a drywall box, routing wiring through an attic with locator rods, mounting a 20‑pound-rated plastic junction box with swing-out brackets, splicing connections with wire nuts, and installing an LED-compatible dimmer. The hosts emphasize safe practices (power off, accessible junction box with blank cover), careful measurement to center the fixture in the largest area rather than over the bed, and testing the system after power restoration. The narrative provides concrete on-site techniques for planning, mounting, wiring, and testing an overhead fixture in a real bedroom scenario.
